expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription; each with a literal `status` field

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: CanceledSubscription = { status: "canceled"; cancelReason: string; voluntary: boolean; } — no trialEndDate

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Only a comment: "// If you forget a case, TypeScript warns (with exhaustiveness check)" — no assertNever or never arm is written; the switch omits "active" and "canceled" cases entirely

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: No ID fields or branded types appear anywhere; cancelReason remains a bare `string`

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Only `handleSubscription` (a read-only switch) is shown; no transition function or allowed-transition constraint

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "nothing stops you from reading `trialEndDate` on a canceled subscription" and "sub.cancelReason is a type error" in the trialing branch

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Recommends discriminated union; optionals mentioned only as the anti-pattern: "A flat type with optional fields ... compiles but fails at runtime"
